title: Check yourself: what each server test can see

questions.stem: A participant reads the request with ctx.get("Request"). Its unit test builds the Context with ctx.put("Request", purchase), calls prepare, and passes. What does the participant find when the server first runs it?

options.text: It finds no request, since IncomingListener stores the request under another key
options.says: IncomingListener stores the request under "REQUEST"; the hand-built Context shared the participant's wrong key, so only a Context from the real listener shows it

options.text: It finds no request, since IncomingListener queues the Context only after prepare has run
options.says: the listener puts the Context on the queue before any session takes it; the key is the problem

options.text: It finds the request, since Context keys are matched without regard to case
options.says: the Context is a map; "Request" and "REQUEST" are different keys

options.text: It finds the request, since the unit test has already exercised the key it reads
options.says: the test used the same wrong key as the participant, so it agreed with it instead of with production

origin.section: 11.1 A Participant Test Gets Its Context From `IncomingListener`

questions.stem: A test class starts Q2 once. In setConfiguration, a velocity participant gets its per-card counter from the NameRegistrar. To give every test clean counts, a @BeforeEach method registers a new counter object under the counter's name. A test that expects a card's first purchase to pass gets a refusal, because the card already has purchases from an earlier test. Why?

options.text: The participant keeps the object it found at start-up, so it never counts in the new one
options.says: the lookup happened once, in setConfiguration; registering a new object changes the registry, not the participant's field

options.text: The participant keeps a copy of each count it has seen, so it writes them into the new one
options.says: nothing copies the counts; the participant simply still holds the first object

options.text: The registry refuses a second object under a name already in use, so the first counter stays registered
options.says: NameRegistrar.register replaces the entry; the participant just never looks again

options.text: The registry keeps one object per test class, so the new counter is only seen by the next class
options.says: the NameRegistrar is one map per JVM, shared by every class and test

origin.section: 11.3 Tests That Share a Q2 Share Its State

questions.stem: A server's 50_server.xml names NACChannel. The network's specification says terminals send four ASCII digits of length before each message. The integration test starts Q2 on the shipped descriptors and connects a client built with the channel class and packager that 50_server.xml names, and every purchase is approved. What does that test tell you about the terminals in the field?

options.text: Nothing about their framing, since its client would agree with 50_server.xml whatever that file named
options.says: a client copied from the descriptor matches it by construction; only a client built from the network's specification tests it

options.text: Nothing about their framing, since a socket test checks the packager but never the channel
options.says: a socket test goes through the channel as well; the problem is that this client's channel was copied from the server

options.text: That they will be answered, since its purchases reached the channel in 50_server.xml over a real socket
options.says: a real socket tests the framing the client uses, and this client uses the server's, not the terminals'

options.text: That they will be answered, since QServer detects the framing of each new connection
options.says: the server reads with the channel its descriptor names; a frame it can't read ends the connection

origin.section: 11.4 Only a Socket Test With the Terminals' Framing Tests `50_server.xml`

questions.stem: A participant keeps the card number in a field from prepare to commit. The suite sends 400 purchases, one after another, through a TransactionManager with four sessions, and every answer and every journal line is right. Why did the suite miss the bug?

options.text: Each purchase ended before the next one began, so no other transaction wrote the field in between
options.says: the field is overwritten only while another transaction is inside the same participant; one at a time never overlaps

options.text: Each purchase ended before the next one began, so each one ran in a freshly created participant and field
options.says: the TransactionManager creates one participant instance and every session uses it

options.text: The four sessions ran the purchases side by side, so the field needs more writers than that to go wrong
options.says: requests sent one after another are never side by side; two transactions in flight are enough

options.text: The four sessions ran the purchases side by side, so each session kept a field of its own
options.says: sessions share the one participant instance and its fields

origin.section: 11.5 Only Two Transactions in Flight Show What Sessions Share
